statement: Grouped SHAP values and accumulated local effects describe how a model turns measures into estimates, not what changing a measure would do; within a group of correlated inputs the split of credit is arbitrary, and one input's share is said to be unstable when the reseeds' rank correlation is under 0.7.
claimed_basis: Lundberg & Lee 2017; Apley & Zhu 2020; Molnar et al. 2022

statement: The distribution of single-day 24-hour recall intakes, or of each person's mean of two recalls, is wider than the distribution of usual (long-run average) intake, so percentiles and the share below a cut-off read from it are wrong in both tails; the NCI measurement-error model is needed and the mean-of-days distribution is ranked lower and shown only beside it, labeled.
regime: inference purpose, dietary lens; a nutrient or food with repeated 24-h recalls on at least a subset (>=2 people with >=2 recalls)
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §03 ('Averaging 2 days leaves too much within-person variance in the distribution; the tails are too fat'); Tooze et al. 2006, 2010

statement: Results wording starts at the design's floor, an association for an observational design; causal wording is offered only for trials, 'an estimated effect, its assumptions named' only when no standing question points elsewhere and no stated assumption is refuted, and model explanations are never worded as effects.
decision: the drafted wordings and the noticing on stronger user wording

statement: Under inference, losing more than 10% of the rows to complete-case analysis is enough to warrant a concern, shown with a comparison of the kept and dropped rows' outcome and predictors.
regime: inference; complete-case strategy; share of rows dropped > 0.10
decision: concern on the fit (complete-case row loss)
claimed_basis: CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK anti-pattern 1 ('Flag when listwise deletion drops >10% of rows')

statement: Under the fit and its imputation model a predictor with exactly two values needs no code-or-amount answer, because coding it as one indicator or as a numeric amount gives the same slope, interval and every prediction (only the intercept's reference changes), and both imputation models fill it as a yes/no; when a unit's rows are combined the two readings differ (mean = a share vs the most frequent value), so there it is asked.
decision: Whether the fit waits for a two-valued predictor's coding answer.
claimed_basis: Docstring reasoning only (readings.py:1600-1608); methods.imputation.column_kind (imputation.py:127) imputes any two-valued numeric column as binary.

statement: For the difference between two families' cross-validated scores on 10 repeats of 5 folds, the ordinary paired t on the rK − 1 = 49 degrees of freedom over the 50 fold differences, t = mean(d)/√(s²_d/(rK)), gives an approximately valid 95% interval, because repeating the folds 10 times makes the fold differences approximately independent.
regime: comparing two families' cross-validated scores on a repeated k-fold substrate (10 × 5), any outcome
claimed_basis: RECIPES §3.7 comparison table; Dietterich 1998 (Neural Computation 10:1895); Bouckaert & Frank, PAKDD 2004.

statement: When a time-varying confounder was itself affected by earlier exposure, a standard regression that adjusts for the confounder at every time point gives an unbiased estimate of the total effect of the exposure history, so marginal structural models are needed only to gain efficiency.
regime: longitudinal exposure with a time-varying confounder affected by earlier exposure

statement: When a unit's rows are repeated measurements of one quantity, averaging k of them cuts within-person variance k-fold.
regime: repeated rows answered 'repeats' (e.g., 24-hour recalls); aggregation by mean; k = the median rows per unit

statement: sd(r_i)/√n_sim over the simulated units' final risks bounds the g-formula's Monte Carlo error from above.
decision: the methods text's Monte Carlo error

statement: When a unit's rows repeat, feature-wise intervals that treat rows as independent would be too narrow, so the tests use CR2 with Bell-McCaffrey degrees of freedom, and above 200 exposures (CR2 computed per exposure) the intervals are refused rather than reported as independent.
regime: inference; feature-wise family; clustered rows; more than 200 exposures for the refusal
claimed_basis: none stated beyond the sentence (CR2 / Bell–McCaffrey from the math layer, inference.cr2).

statement: Total energy's unit is settled by its values only when its median ratio to the macronutrients' Atwater reconstruction lies within 0.90-1.10 (kcal, over the same days the macronutrients span); a ratio within 5% of 4.184 x N or of N (N >= 2) could be kJ or an N-day kcal total (a 4-day kcal total reads 4.00, within 5% of kJ's 4.184), so the unit and the day count are asked together with the fitting readings offered, and a ratio near 1 never settles how many days the values span.
regime: Dietary data with total energy and at least two macronutrient totals in grams.
decision: Energy unit/day count used by intake screens and energy methods.
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §01 (Atwater reconstruction; pass band 0.90-1.10); RATIO_TOLERANCE 0.05 = 'the pack's band around the kJ factor (nutrition._reconstruct)'; fifth gate (a 4-day record).

statement: For boosted trees (scikit-learn's HistGradientBoosting) and XGBoost under prediction, when the effective size of one outer training fold (n_plan: units for a numeric outcome; units in the rarest class for a yes/no or class outcome) is below 300, fitting once at the library's default settings with no search (HistGB: learning rate 0.1, 31 leaves, smallest leaf 20, no L2, 100 trees; XGBoost: learning rate 0.3, depth 6, child weight 1, λ 1, 100 rounds) predicts at least as well as nested tuning and is better calibrated, because settings ranked on so few units vary from sample to sample and miscalibrate.
regime: Prediction; boosted trees and XGBoost; n_plan < 300 (e.g. fewer than 375 events in the training set at K = 5); any outcome type
decision: Tuning plan below n_eff 300: no Sobol candidates (S = 0); the library defaults are the only candidate
claimed_basis: RECIPES §4.6: 'The reason is the variance of the chosen settings, not optimism' (Riley et al. 2021; Van Calster et al. 2020; Martin et al. 2021); '300 is a convention'; standard_source "scikit-learn's defaults" (boosted trees) and "XGBoost's defaults" (XGBoost).
